transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because for the past few weeks I’ve just had this heavy sadness sitting on me most of the day. It’s like this pressure I can’t shake. I’m a nurse, so at work I’m still smiling and talking to patients, you know, doing what I’m supposed to do… and sometimes I’ll catch myself worrying about whether they can tell. But inside I feel like I’m barely keeping it together.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings been present every day, or do they come and go?

It’s been… about three weeks, I think. Pretty much since right after I found out I was pregnant. I keep thinking maybe I should be more excited, and then I get stuck thinking about work and telling people and all of that—but yeah, the feeling has been there most days, like it doesn’t really let up much.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with loved ones?

Yeah… I mean, I used to have things I’d do after shifts to kind of reset—like painting, or I’d go to yoga, and sometimes salsa, though I was never that good at it, honestly. There was this one class where I kept stepping on this woman’s foot and we both just started laughing, and normally I’d love that kind of thing.

But lately I just… go home and sit on the couch. My phone will buzz and I know it’s probably friends checking in or asking me to come out, and I just ignore it because answering feels like too much. None of it feels worth the effort right now.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or having less energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I… I’m not totally sure. I mean, work is tiring anyway, being on my feet and doing rounds and all that, and sometimes I wonder if I’m just blaming everything on that. Like yesterday I came home and just stood in the kitchen staring at this mug I was supposed to wash, and then I started thinking about how I need to reorganize the whole cabinet because nothing fits right anymore…

Sorry, I don’t know if that answers it. I guess I haven’t really been paying attention to whether it’s energy exactly. It’s more like I’m just… not doing much when I get home.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… I think I’m eating less. I know I should be eating regularly, especially now, and it makes me feel kind of guilty, but most days food just sounds… unappealing.

Like at the clinic I’ll tell myself I’ll grab something after the next patient, and then it’s halfway through the shift and I realize I’ve only had coffee or some crackers from my bag. I used to be better about packing actual meals—those little containers, you know, trying to be organized—but lately I just don’t really want anything. I haven’t been tracking my weight or anything, though.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping more than usual?

I don’t know… I haven’t really been keeping track. I mean, sleep’s been weird maybe, but my schedule can be kind of all over the place anyway, and sometimes I stay up because I get stuck watching these random videos—like home organization ones, which is funny because my own place is not organized at all.

But as far as like, falling asleep or staying asleep… I’m not sure. I guess I haven’t noticed it in a clear way.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety in a way that’s unusual for you?

Yeah… slowed down, I think. Not really fidgety. It’s more like everything takes me longer than it should, like I’m moving through syrup or something.

At the clinic, even basic stuff—like gathering wound supplies, or finishing charting—feels like it takes me forever. And then I get annoyed with myself because it’s not complicated, I’ve done it a million times. I’ll be standing there looking for gauze and saline, and then I start thinking about how the supply room is arranged badly, and how someone should really label the bins better… but the actual point is, yeah, I’m slower. Noticeably slower.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… that’s actually part of why I finally said something at my prenatal appointment. I kind of… I didn’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m not sitting there with a plan or anything like that. But I’ve had these thoughts like, I wish I just wouldn’t wake up.

And then I feel awful even saying that, because—sorry, this is probably not the point—but you’re supposed to be excited and taking care of yourself, and I know all the things I’d tell a patient if they said that to me. But when it’s me, it’s like I keep trying to explain it away or tell myself I’m just tired.

So… yes. Not a plan to hurt myself, but those thoughts have been there, and they scared me.
